title: Real gases are not quite ideal
caption: The compression factor Z = pV/nRT is exactly 1 for an ideal gas. For a real gas such as methane, attractions pull Z below 1 at moderate pressure; at high pressure the molecules' own volume pushes it above 1. The curve is illustrative.
alt: Z against pressure: a flat line at 1 for an ideal gas; a real-gas curve dipping to about 0.8 near 250 atm and rising above 1 beyond about 500 atm.
description: Ideal gas: Z = 1 at every pressure.
Real gas: Z falls below 1 (attractions dominate), reaches a minimum, then rises above 1 (molecular volume dominates).
